title: Roblox must make changes after failing to block adults creeping on kids
gist: Australia's eSafety Commissioner found Roblox's child-safety defaults still allowed adult strangers to contact and search for kids, forcing Roblox into a court-enforceable undertaking with mandatory third-party auditing of both its safety controls and its in-house AI age-estimation system.

insights.claim: Australia's eSafety Commissioner testing found that Roblox's child profiles, connection lists, and forum activity remained visible and contactable by adult strangers platform-wide, despite Roblox's fall-2025 messaging safeguards, with no parental alerts triggered by such contact.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Concrete regulator-verified evidence that Roblox's existing child-safety controls have material gaps, raising compliance and reputational risk for the platform among advertisers and parents.
insights.quote: profiles and biographies, including account names, number and names of connections, avatar images, and non-sensitive biographical information such as their interests were visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, with no option to restrict the visibility of this information.
insights.locator: eSafety conducted testing earlier this year that flagged alarming gaps

insights.claim: Roblox has entered a court-enforceable undertaking with Australia's eSafety Commissioner to overhaul child-safety defaults within three months, and it marks the first time Australia has required third-party auditing of a platform since the Online Safety Act became enforceable.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Sets a regulatory precedent for mandatory third-party AI/safety-system auditing that other jurisdictions (UK, EU) could replicate against gaming and social platforms.
insights.locator: has entered a court-enforceable agreement to make changes in the next three months

insights.claim: eSafety warned Roblox in October 2025 that it was prepared to seek penalties of up to $49.5 million under the Online Safety Act for exploitation and grooming failures, giving the regulator real financial leverage beyond this settlement.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Quantifies the tail-risk fine exposure Roblox faces if the current remediation plan fails an audit, a downside scenario investors should track.
insights.quote: seeking penalties of up to $49.5 million
insights.locator: Last October, eSafety warned that it was prepared to

insights.claim: Roblox's in-house Facial Age Estimation system has processed 338 million age-check records and, per the company's own testing against human-reviewer consensus, matches the correct age band for adults more than 80 percent of the time.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: An 80 percent agreement rate implies meaningful mislabeling risk at Roblox's scale; the newly agreed third-party audit could expose weaknesses that force costly remediation or damage user trust.
insights.quote: the model's age-band estimate agrees with the human consensus label for adults more than 80 percent of the time
insights.locator: tests that compared the model 'against independent ground truth'

insights.claim: Roblox itself cautions that 'a single accuracy number is not very meaningful' for its age-estimation system, since quality also depends on ranking quality, calibration, and stability near age-band boundaries.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Roblox's own hedging on its headline accuracy statistic is a signal that the true error rate near critical age boundaries (e.g., minors vs. adults) may be understated by the topline figure.
insights.quote: a single accuracy number is not very meaningful
insights.locator: the platform hedged a bit when discussing how it sorts users

insights.claim: Roblox became the first large online gaming platform to require facial age checks in January 2026, but the biometric selfies submitted may be retained for up to 30 days, creating breach exposure even though Roblox says it usually auto-deletes them.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A privacy/security tradeoff investors and regulators should weigh: biometric retention creates data-breach liability even while addressing child-safety optics.
insights.locator: it may retain that data for up to 30 days

insights.claim: Roblox is used by 1.7 million Australian children and is the country's second most popular online game for kids, giving the eSafety enforcement action outsized reach relative to a niche platform.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Scale of the affected user base underscores why this case is a bellwether rather than a minor compliance action.
insights.locator: the online gaming platform—which 1.7 million Australian kids use

insights.claim: eSafety plans to release a transparency report later in 2026 detailing how successful online gaming platforms broadly have been at mitigating child-safety harms, extending regulatory scrutiny beyond Roblox to the wider gaming industry.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Signals a coming sector-wide regulatory disclosure event that could affect reputational and compliance-cost expectations for other gaming platforms with large child user bases.
insights.locator: Later this year, eSafety will release a transparency report
